resources.string: Add TouchQuell to Quick Settings for one-tap touch control.
Swipe down twice, tap Edit, then drag TouchQuell into Quick Settings.
TouchQuell is ready in Quick Settings.
TouchQuell was added to Quick Settings
TouchQuell is already in Quick Settings
The TouchQuell tile was not added
%1$s for the next block. An active block keeps its original release key.
On Android 14 or newer, enable TouchQuell in Accessibility to block touch without root.
Rootless mode is ready. Use a volume key to release touch.
TouchQuell is enabled and waiting for its Accessibility service to connect.
Touch exploration is active, so TouchQuell must use its root fallback.
Another Accessibility service is filtering hardware keys, so TouchQuell must use its root fallback.
Power cannot reliably release rootless mode, so TouchQuell must use its root fallback.
Rootless mode requires Android 14 or newer.
Pauses touchscreen input until the selected volume key is pressed.
TouchQuell captures touchscreen motion only while touch is paused. It never reads screen content. Press the selected volume key to restore touch.
For an APK installed outside an app store, Android may first require App info → More → Allow restricted settings. Then enable TouchQuell in Accessibility.
Root and root-manager approval are required on Android 13 or older, for the Power release key, or when rootless capture is unavailable. TouchQuell requests root only when needed.
TouchQuell could not start root touch blocking. Check root access and try again.
TouchQuell is not ready yet. Wait for its Accessibility service to connect, then try again.
TouchQuell collects or transmits no personal data and never reads screen content. The app is GPL-3.0-or-later; its bundled blockevent helper is Apache-2.0. Source: github.com/bzhangj13zzz/touchquell
